claim_traces.claim_title: Humans only use 10% of their brains
claim_traces.claim_text: "Humans only use 10% of their brain capacity — the other 90% remains dormant and untapped."
reasoning_steps: The claim that humans only use 10% of their brain capacity is a well-known scientific myth

Neuroimaging techniques such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and positron emission tomography (PET) demonstrate that virtually all areas of the brain are active and have designated functions throughout the course of a day, even during sleep

Furthermore, evolutionary biology and clinical neurology show that unutilized brain tissue would atrophy or be selected against, and damage to even minute regions of the brain almost always results in measurable functional deficits.
